Because it generates optimized numerical code for hardware ISAs, libraries, and vector targets, it fits the compiler-style kernel optimization category, though outside ML.

title: TaintEMU: Decoupling Tracking from Functional Domains for Architecture-Agnostic and Efficient Whole-System Taint Tracking
authors: Lei Cui (Guangxi Normal University), Youquan Xian (Guangxi Normal University), Peng Liu (Guangxi Normal University), Longjin Lu (Independent Researcher)
rationale: TaintEMU improves whole-system taint tracking by decoupling functional and tracking domains in QEMU, mapping shadow registers, and generating host tracking instructions. This is security analysis/emulation infrastructure rather than an optimization of application compute kernels.

title: Segue & ColorGuard: Optimizing SFI Performance and Scalability on Modern Architectures
authors: Shravan Narayan (UT Austin), Tal Garfinkel (UC San Diego), Evan Johnson (UC San Diego), Zachary Yedidia (Stanford University), Yingchen Wang (UC Berkeley), Andrew Brown (Intel), Anjo Vahldiek-Oberwagner (Intel Labs), Michael LeMay (Intel Labs), Wenyong Huang (Intel), Xin Wang (Intel), Mingqiu Sun (Intel), Dean Tullsen (UC San Diego), Deian Stefan (UC San Diego)
rationale: The full text describes Segue as using x86-64 segmentation to reduce SFI instrumentation cost and ColorGuard as using memory tagging/MPK to pack more Wasm instances. These are isolation and runtime/toolchain optimizations for memory safety and scalability, not compute-kernel optimizations under the census definition.

title: Pave: Information Flow Control for Privacy-preserving Online Data Processing Services
authors: Minkyung Park (University of Texas at Dallas), Jaeseung Choi (Sogang University), Hyeonmin Lee (University of Virginia), Taekyoung Kwon (Seoul National University)
rationale: The full text presents Pave as an SGX-based information-flow-control framework with a PaveBox runtime monitor, formal non-interference model, and prototype evaluation. Its mechanisms enforce privacy and syscall-flow constraints rather than optimizing compute kernels.

title: EDM: An Ultra-Low Latency Ethernet Fabric for Memory Disaggregation
authors: Weigao Su (Purdue University), Vishal Shrivastav (Purdue University)
rationale: EDM implements a low-latency Ethernet fabric and in-PHY scheduler for memory disaggregation. The contribution is network fabric/protocol hardware design and scheduling, not a compute kernel or kernel compiler.

title: Performance Prediction of On-NIC Network Functions with Multi-Resource Contention and Traffic Awareness
authors: Shaofeng Wu (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Qiang Su (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Zhixiong Niu (Microsoft Research), Hong Xu (The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
rationale: Yala predicts performance interference among network functions co-running on SmartNICs using resource-contention and traffic models. This is performance modeling and resource-management support, not kernel-style optimization.

title: Gigaflow: Pipeline-Aware Sub-Traversal Caching for Modern SmartNICs
authors: Annus Zulfiqar (University of Michigan), Ali Imran (University of Michigan), Venkat Kunaparaju (Purdue University), Ben Pfaff (Feldera Inc.), Gianni Antichi (Politecnico di Milano), Muhammad Shahbaz (University of Michigan)
rationale: Gigaflow accelerates SmartNIC vSwitch packet processing with pipeline-aware sub-traversal caching of flow-rule segments. The contribution is network-stack/NIC caching infrastructure, not a compute kernel, fusion, precision, layout, or kernel compiler contribution.

title: TNIC: A Trusted NIC Architecture
authors: Dimitra Giantsidi (The University of Edinburgh), Julian Pritzi (Technical University of Munich), Felix Gust (Technical University of Munich), Antonios Katsarakis (Huawei Research), Atsushi Koshiba (Technical University of Munich), Pramod Bhatotia (Technical University of Munich)
rationale: TNIC is a trusted NIC architecture and network stack for Byzantine cloud environments with a formally verified root of trust. Its focus is security architecture and distributed systems support, not optimized compute kernels.

title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
authors: Alexander Breuer (Friedrich Schiller University Jena), Mark Blacher (Friedrich Schiller University Jena), Max Engel (Friedrich Schiller University Jena), Joachim Giesen (Friedrich Schiller University Jena), Alexander Heinecke (Intel Corporation), Julien Klaus (Friedrich Schiller University Jena), Stefan Remke (Friedrich Schiller University Jena)
rationale: Einsum Trees introduces an IR for globally optimizing data layout across an einsum contraction path so tensor expressions execute more efficiently. Data-layout planning for tensor-expression execution is kernel-style scheduling/layout work, with a compiler-IR component.

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference Efficiency through Block Dependency Analysis
authors: Zhanyuan Di (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Leping Wang (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS), En Shao (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Zhaojia Ma (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Ziyi Ren (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Feng Hua (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Lixian Ma (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Jie Zhao (Hunan University), Guangming Tan (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Ninghui Sun (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)
rationale: BlockDepend is an ML compiler framework that extracts block-level dependencies from lower compilation phases to expose parallelization opportunities and improve memory access/GPU utilization for DNN inference. That is compiler-driven kernel-adjacent optimization and scheduling/layout analysis.

title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
authors: Liang Qiao (University of Science and Technology of China), Jun Shi (University of Science and Technology of China), Xiaoyu Hao (University of Science and Technology of China), Xi Fang (University of Science and Technology of China), Sen Zhang (University of Science and Technology of China), Minfan Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China), Ziqi Zhu (University of Science and Technology of China), Junshi Chen (University of Science and Technology of China), Hong An (University of Science and Technology of China), Xulong Tang (University of Pittsburgh), Bing Li (NIO), Honghui Yuan (NIO), Xinyang Wang (NIO)
rationale: Pruner accelerates tensor program tuning in TVM by drafting and verifying schedule candidates with cost models. Because the search output is optimized tensor programs/kernels for GPU platforms, it directly matches the compiler/autotuner kernel-style category.

title: Relax: Composable Abstractions for End-to-End Dynamic Machine Learning
authors: Ruihang Lai (Carnegie Mellon University), Junru Shao (OpenAI), Siyuan Feng (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Steven Lyubomirsky (NVIDIA), Bohan Hou (Carnegie Mellon University), Wuwei Lin (OpenAI), Zihao Ye (University of Washington), Hongyi Jin (Carnegie Mellon University), Yuchen Jin (Hyperbolic), Jiawei Liu (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Lesheng Jin (Hyperbolic), Yaxing Cai (NVIDIA), Ziheng Jiang (ByteDance), Yong Wu (NVIDIA), Sunghyun Park (NVIDIA), Prakalp Srivastava (Netflix), Jared Roesch (NVIDIA), Todd C. Mowry (Carnegie Mellon University), Tianqi Chen (Carnegie Mellon University,NVIDIA)
rationale: Relax is a compiler abstraction and AOT framework for dynamic-shape ML that unifies graphs, loop-level tensor programs, and external library calls. The introduction explicitly cites dynamic-shape-aware operator fusion, tensor-program optimizations, and code generation across backends.

title: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications with Ayo
authors: Xin Tan (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Yimin Jiang (Unaffiliated), Yitao Yang (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Hong Xu (The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
rationale: Ayo/Teola optimizes end-to-end LLM application workflows with primitive-level dataflow orchestration and topology-aware batching. These are application orchestration and request scheduling techniques above the kernel layer.

title: PAPI: Exploiting Dynamic Parallelism in Large Language Model Decoding with a Processing-In-Memory-Enabled Computing System
authors: Yintao He (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Haiyu Mao (King's College London,ETH Zürich), Christina Giannoula (University of Toronto,Vector Institute), Mohammad Sadrosadati (ETH Zürich), Juan Gómez-Luna (NVIDIA), Huawei Li (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Xiaowei Li (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Ying Wang (SKLP, Institute of Computing Technology, CAS), Onur Mutlu (ETH Zürich)
rationale: PAPI proposes a PIM-enabled heterogeneous architecture and runtime scheduling of LLM decoding kernels to GPU or PIM units. Under the codebook's hardware-architecture rule, this simulated architecture/scheduling work is not a software-realizable kernel-style optimization.

title: PIM is All You Need: A CXL-Enabled GPU-Free System for LLM Inference
authors: Yufeng Gu (University of Michigan), Alireza Khadem (University of Michigan), Sumanth Umesh (University of Michigan), Ning Liang (University of Michigan), Xavier Servot (ETH Zurich), Onur Mutlu (ETH Zurich), Ravi Iyer (Google), Reetuparna Das (University of Michigan)
rationale: CENT is a CXL-enabled, PIM-based GPU-free system for LLM inference that addresses memory bandwidth and capacity limits. The primary contribution is a hardware/system architecture rather than a new software compute kernel or compiler for existing hardware.

title: Be CIM or Be Memory: A Dual-mode-aware DNN Compiler for CIM Accelerators
authors: Shixin Zhao (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Yuming Li (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Bing Li (Institute of Microelectronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Yintao He (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences,University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Mengdi Wang (State Key Lab of Processors, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Yinhe Han (State Key Lab of Processors, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences), Ying Wang (State Key Lab of Processors, Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
rationale: CMSwitch is a DNN compiler that optimizes resource allocation and compute/memory mode switching for CIM accelerators. Its compilation output schedules meta-operators and resource layouts for DNN execution, matching compiler-driven scheduling/layout optimization.

title: RTL Verification for Secure Speculation Using Contract Shadow Logic
authors: Qinhan Tan (Princeton University), Yuheng Yang (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Thomas Bourgeat (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne), Sharad Malik (Princeton University), Mengjia Yan (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)
rationale: Contract Shadow Logic improves RTL verification scalability for secure speculation properties. The work verifies hardware security contracts and does not propose compute kernels or a kernel-generating optimization system.

title: ElasticMiter: Formally Verified Dataflow Circuit Rewrites
authors: Ayatallah Elakhras (EPFL), Jiahui Xu (ETH Zurich), Martin Erhart (ETH Zurich), Paolo Ienne (EPFL), Lana Josipovic (ETH Zurich)
rationale: The full text defines latency-insensitive equivalence, builds the ElasticMiter verifier, and uses it to verify HLS dataflow-circuit rewrite rules. Although the rewrite pass can reduce FPGA area/latency, the primary contribution is formal verification and circuit rewriting for HLS, not software kernel-style optimization for existing compute workloads.

title: Robustness Verification for Checking Crash Consistency of Non-volatile Memory
authors: Zhilei Han (School of Software, Tsinghua University), Fei He (School of Software, Tsinghua University)
rationale: PMVerify is an automated robustness verifier for crash consistency of non-volatile-memory programs, using symbolic encoding and SMT solving. The work is correctness verification for persistent memory, not compute-kernel optimization.

title: Hardware Sentinel: Protecting Software Applications from Hardware Silent Data Corruptions
authors: Rhea Dutta (Meta Platforms, Inc.), Harish Dattatraya Dixit (Meta Platforms, Inc.), Rik Van Riel (Meta Platforms, Inc.), Gautham Vunnam (Meta Platforms, Inc.), Sriram Sankar (Meta Platforms, Inc.)
rationale: Hardware Sentinel detects hardware silent data corruptions from software failure indicators across a large datacenter fleet. Its contribution is monitoring and diagnosis infrastructure rather than kernels, fusion, numeric formats, or compiler-generated kernels.

title: MDPeek: Breaking Balanced Branches in SGX with Memory Disambiguation Unit Side Channels
authors: Chang Liu (Tsinghua University), Shuaihu Feng (Zhongguancun Laboratory), Yuan Li (Zhongguancun Laboratory), Dongsheng Wang (Tsinghua University), Wenjian He (Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.), Yongqiang Lyu (Tsinghua University), Trevor E. Carlson (National University of Singapore)
rationale: MDPeek is a side-channel attack and mitigation for Intel SGX that reverse engineers the Memory Disambiguation Unit and demonstrates attacks on SGX-secured applications. The contribution is security analysis and defense, not a compute kernel, kernel generator, or kernel-level ML optimization.

title: Accelerating Number Theoretic Transform with Multi-GPU Systems for Efficient Zero Knowledge Proof
authors: Zhuoran Ji (School of Cyber Science and Technology, Shandong University), Jianyu Zhao (School of Cyber Science and Technology, Shandong University), Peimin Gao (School of Cyber Science and Technology, Shandong University), Xiangkai Yin (School of Cyber Science and Technology, Shandong University), Lei Ju (Quan Cheng Laboratory)
rationale: UniNTT accelerates the Number Theoretic Transform on multi-GPU systems with a recursive decomposition that maps NTT computation across warp, thread-block, GPU, and multi-GPU hierarchy levels. This is a hardware-aware optimization of a core GPU compute primitive.

title: BatchZK: A Fully Pipelined GPU-Accelerated System for Batch Generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
authors: Tao Lu (Zhejiang University,National University of Singapore), Yuxun Chen (Zhejiang University), Zonghui Wang (Zhejiang University), Xiaohang Wang (Zhejiang University), Wenzhi Chen (Zhejiang University), Jiaheng Zhang (National University of Singapore)
rationale: BatchZK proposes a fully pipelined GPU-accelerated proof generation system whose contributions include pipelined GPU execution for Merkle tree, sum-check, and linear-time encoder modules. The work maps cryptographic computational modules to continuously occupied GPU threads and overlaps transfer with computation, which is a kernel-level scheduling and compute-primitive optimization.

title: UniZK: Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proof with Unified Hardware and Flexible Kernel Mapping
authors: Cheng Wang (Xi'an Jiaotong University,Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Core Technology), Mingyu Gao (Tsinghua University,Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute)
rationale: UniZK proposes a unified ZKP accelerator architecture with systolic-array hardware, extra links, vector processing, and mapping strategies for that hardware. Under the codebook's hardware-architecture rule, this remains outside kernel-style optimization because the central contribution is a new accelerator rather than software kernels for existing hardware.

title: Concurrency-Informed Orchestration for Serverless Functions
authors: Qichang Liu (University of Virginia), Yue Cheng (University of Virginia), Haiying Shen (University of Virginia), Ao Wang (Alibaba Group), Bharathan Balaji (Amazon)
rationale: CIDRE is a serverless function container orchestration algorithm that chooses between delayed warm starts and cold starts and makes concurrency-informed eviction decisions. Its contributions are scheduling and resource-management policies above the kernel level.

title: Dilu: Enabling GPU Resourcing-on-Demand for Serverless DL Serving via Introspective Elasticity
authors: Cunchi Lv (ICT, CAS,UCAS), Xiao Shi (ICT, CAS,Nanjing Institute of InforSuperBahn), Zhengyu Lei (ICT, CAS,UCAS), Jinyue Huang (ICT, CAS, UCAS), Wenting Tan (ICT, CAS), Xiaohui Zheng (ICT, CAS), Xiaofang Zhao (ICT, CAS,IICT, Suzhou, CAS)
rationale: Dilu is a cross-layer serverless DL system for introspective elasticity, profiling, scheduling, and adaptive two-dimensional GPU resource scaling. These mechanisms allocate and co-scale GPU resources for DL tasks but do not propose new kernels or kernel-level code generation.

title: Medusa: Accelerating Serverless LLM Inference with Materialization
authors: Shaoxun Zeng (Tsinghua University), Minhui Xie (Tsinghua University), Shiwei Gao (Tsinghua University), Youmin Chen (Tsinghua University), Youyou Lu (Tsinghua University)
rationale: Medusa reduces serverless LLM cold-start latency by materializing CUDA graphs and KV-cache initialization state offline and restoring them online. The kernel-address restoration mechanisms support runtime state recovery, but the primary contribution is serving/runtime materialization rather than new compute kernels.

title: Virgo: Cluster-level Matrix Unit Integration in GPUs for Scalability and Energy Efficiency
authors: Hansung Kim (University of California, Berkeley), Ruohan Richard Yan (University of California, Berkeley), Joshua You (University of California, Berkeley), Tieliang Vamber Yang (NVIDIA Corporation), Yakun Sophia Shao (University of California, Berkeley)
rationale: Virgo proposes a GPU microarchitecture that disaggregates matrix units at the SIMT core-cluster level and evaluates it using synthesizable RTL. The paper discusses mapping fused DNN workloads, but the primary artifact is a hardware architecture rather than a software-realizable kernel or compiler on existing devices.

title: Aqua: Network-Accelerated Memory Offloading for LLMs in Scale-Up GPU Domains
authors: Abhishek Vijaya Kumar (Cornell University), Gianni Antichi (Politecnico di Milano), Rachee Singh (Cornell University)
rationale: Aqua is a GPU memory management framework that reduces paging overhead for preemptive LLM inference by offloading inference state over scale-up interconnects. This is serving-time memory management and scheduling above kernels, not a new kernel or compiler-generated kernel.

title: Optimizing Datalog for the GPU
authors: Yihao Sun (Syracuse University), Ahmedur Rahman Shovon (University of Illinois, Chicago), Thomas Gilray (Washington State University), Sidharth Kumar (University of Illinois, Chicago), Kristopher Micinski (Syracuse University)
rationale: GPUlog is a GPU Datalog backend built from iterated relational-algebra kernels over the HISA data structure. The contribution explicitly implements and optimizes GPU kernels/data structures for Datalog execution, making it kernel-style even though the workload is non-ML.

title: AnyKey: A Key-Value SSD for All Workload Types
authors: Chanyoung Park (Hanyang University), Jungho Lee (Hanyang University), Chun-Yi Liu (Micron Technology Inc.), Kyungtae Kang (Hanyang Univeristy), Mahmut Taylan Kandemir (Pennsylvania State University), Wonil Choi (Hanyang University)
rationale: AnyKey is a KV-SSD design that keeps metadata from growing under varying key sizes and improves storage-device performance across KV workloads. The contribution is storage architecture and metadata organization, not compute kernels or kernel-generation tooling.

title: Simplifying and Accelerating NOR Flash I/O Stack for RAM-Restricted Microcontrollers
authors: Hao Huang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Yanqi Pan (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Wen Xia (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Xiangyu Zou (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Darong Yang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Liang Shi (East China Normal University), Hongwei Du (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen)
rationale: NF2FS is a NOR-flash-friendly file system that changes data organization and wear leveling to coarse file granularity using an all-logging layout. Its optimizations are in the storage I/O stack for microcontrollers, outside the kernel-style compute-optimization construct.

title: Velosiraptor: Code Synthesis for Memory Translation
authors: Reto Achermann (University of British Columbia), Em Chu (JuliaHub), Ryan Mehri (Replit), Ilias Karimalis (University of British Columbia), Margo Seltzer (University of British Columbia)
rationale: Velosiraptor synthesizes verified low-level OS code for configuring memory translation and protection hardware. Its output is OS memory-management code and hardware components, not compute kernels for ML or accelerator workloads.

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
authors: Ramya Prabhu (Microsoft Research), Ajay Nayak (Indian Institute of Science), Jayashree Mohan (Microsoft Research), Ramachandran Ramjee (Microsoft Research), Ashish Panwar (Microsoft Research)
rationale: vAttention uses CUDA virtual memory management to keep the KV cache virtually contiguous while avoiding physical-memory fragmentation. The approach is a memory-management design that reuses existing attention kernels out of the box, so it is above-kernel rather than a new kernel-style optimization.

title: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
authors: Konstantinos Kanellopoulos (ETH Zürich), Konstantinos Sgouras (ETH Zürich), Nisa Bostanci (ETH Zürich), Andreas Kosmas Kakolyris (ETH Zürich), Berkin Kerim Konar (ETH Zürich), Rahul Bera (ETH Zürich), Mohammad Sadrosadati (ETH Zürich), Rakesh Kumar (Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)), Nandita Vijaykumar (University of Toronto), Onur Mutlu (ETH Zürich)
rationale: Virtuoso is a virtual-memory simulation framework with a lightweight userspace OS kernel for evaluating hardware/OS VM schemes. It improves research methodology and simulator accuracy rather than proposing compute kernels or kernel-level optimizations.

title: Instruction-Aware Cooperative TLB and Cache Replacement Policies
authors: Dimitrios Chasapis (Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC)), Georgios Vavouliotis (Unaffiliated), Daniel A. Jiménez (Texas A&M University), Marc Casas (Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC),Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC))
rationale: The full text proposes cooperative STLB and L2 cache replacement policies, iTP and xPTP, for server workloads with large instruction footprints. These are microarchitectural replacement policies evaluated in simulation, not software compute-kernel or compiler-output optimizations.

title: Graph Learning at Scale: Characterizing and Optimizing Pre-Propagation GNNs
rationale: The paper characterizes pre-propagation GNNs and proposes optimized data loading schemes and tailored training methods to improve throughput. These are model-training/data-pipeline optimizations rather than kernel implementations or kernel-generation techniques.

title: SwiftVI: Time-Efficient Planning and Learning with MDPs
rationale: SwiftVI is a suite of value-iteration algorithms for planning and learning with MDPs that prunes actions using priority queues and bounds. The contribution is algorithmic decision-process optimization, not kernel-level compute optimization.

title: Balancing Pipeline Parallelism with Vocabulary Parallelism
rationale: The paper partitions vocabulary layers across pipeline devices and integrates vocabulary parallelism into pipeline schedules to balance computation and memory. This is a distributed training parallelization/scheduling strategy, which the codebook excludes when it does not generate or contribute kernels.

title: Youmu: Efficient Columnar Data Pipeline for LLM Training
rationale: Youmu redesigns the data pipeline so LLM training can consume columnar data directly using page-level I/O and page-level shuffling. The optimization is storage/data loading for training, not a compute kernel or kernel compiler.

title: LeanAttention: Hardware-Aware Scalable Attention Mechanism for the Decode-Phase of Transformers
rationale: I side with coder A: LeanAttention is an optimized exact attention execution mechanism/kernel for transformer decode, while its Stream-K-style work partitioning is the scheduling mechanism behind the kernel.

title: Photon: Federated LLM Pre-Training
rationale: Photon is a federated system for decentralized end-to-end LLM pre-training that reduces communication by combining local parallelism and low-bandwidth Local SGD. Its contributions are distributed training algorithms and system design, not kernel-level optimizations.

title: MEADOW: Memory-efficient Dataflow and Data Packing for Low Power Edge LLMs
rationale: MEADOW proposes a token-parallel head-sequential dataflow and weight-packing execution strategy for LLMs on low-power FPGAs, reducing off-chip memory accesses and latency. This is a hardware-aware dataflow/layout mapping for LLM computation on an existing FPGA platform, so it fits kernel-style scheduling/layout optimization.

title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
rationale: The paper reviews and empirically evaluates existing KV-cache compression techniques and provides tools/measurement guidance for production serving. It does not propose a new precision format implementation, kernel, or kernel-support mechanism itself.

title: Rubick: Exploiting Job Reconfigurability for Deep Learning Cluster Scheduling
rationale: Rubick is a cluster scheduler that co-optimizes DL job execution plans and multi-resource allocation in shared GPU clusters. The contribution is cluster/job scheduling and performance modeling, not kernel-level optimization.

title: SampleAttention: Near-Lossless Acceleration of Long Context LLM Inference with Adaptive Structured Sparse Attention
rationale: SampleAttention replaces dense prefill attention with adaptive structured sparse attention, using query-guided key-value filtering to choose column and slash strips at runtime. Since it proposes an attention variant to accelerate long-context LLM inference, it is kernel-style with scheduling/layout aspects.

title: SPA: SCALING GRAPH NEURAL NETWORK TRAINING ON LARGE GRAPHS VIA PROBABILISTIC SPLITTING
rationale: Spa introduces split parallelism for multi-GPU mini-batch GNN training and a probabilistic partitioning algorithm to reduce redundant sampling, loading, computation, and communication. This is a distributed training parallelism strategy rather than a kernel or kernel generator.

title: SparseTransX: Efficient Training of Translation-Based Knowledge Graph Embeddings Using Sparse Matrix Operations
rationale: SparseTransX replaces core knowledge-graph embedding computations with sparse-dense matrix multiplication kernels, unifying scatter/gather operations as sparse matrix operations. The primary contribution explicitly reformulates and implements sparse kernels on CPU/GPU for training.

title: ReaL: Efficient RLHF Training of Large Language Models with Parameter Reallocation
rationale: ReaL improves RLHF training by searching execution plans and reallocating parameters across a GPU cluster for different RLHF workloads. Its contributions are resource allocation and parallelization strategy, not kernel-level code or numeric kernel support.

title: Interference-aware Edge Runtime Prediction with Conformal Matrix Completion
rationale: Pitot predicts edge workload runtimes using interference-aware matrix completion and conformal uncertainty bounds. This is runtime prediction for resource management, not a compute-kernel optimization.

title: DiffServe: Efficiently Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Query-Aware Model Scaling
rationale: DiffServe constructs diffusion-model cascades, routes queries by difficulty, and dynamically allocates serving resources. The contribution is model-serving policy and resource management above kernels.

title: ProtoRAIL: A Risk-cognizant Imitation Agent for Adaptive vCPU Oversubscription In the Cloud
rationale: ProtoRAIL learns risk-cognizant policies for adaptive vCPU oversubscription in cloud systems using imitation learning and expert refinement. It is a cloud resource-management policy, not a kernel-style compute optimization.

title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
rationale: APOLLO is a memory-efficient LLM optimizer that approximates AdamW-style gradient scaling with low-rank optimizer state and random projection. The contribution is a training algorithm/optimizer, which the codebook excludes absent kernel-level support.

title: AI Metropolis: Scaling Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Simulation with Out-of-order Execution
rationale: AI Metropolis is a simulation engine that schedules LLM-agent simulations using out-of-order execution to avoid false dependencies. It improves simulation/request scheduling rather than proposing LLM kernels or kernel-generation mechanisms.

title: The Hidden Bloat in Machine Learning Systems
rationale: Negativa-ML detects and removes unused CPU and GPU code in ML framework shared libraries, including unused GPU kernels. Removing bloat from binaries is a software maintenance/debloating tool, not a new or improved compute kernel or kernel compiler.

title: PipeFill: Using GPUs During Bubbles in Pipeline-parallel LLM Training
rationale: PipeFill fills pipeline-parallel training bubbles with other pending jobs using bubble instructions, placement, and execution orchestration. This is GPU cluster/job scheduling during idle pipeline periods, not kernel-level optimization.

title: HyC-LoRA: Memory Efficient LoRA Fine-tuning with Hybrid Activation Compression
rationale: I side with coder A: HyC-LoRA makes activation quantization/compression a primary mechanism and implements custom Triton backward/fused operators, so it is precision-format work with kernel support rather than compression only.

title: Radius: Range-based Gradient Sparsity for Large Foundation Model Pre-training
rationale: Radius is a gradient sparsity and communication-compression algorithm for large foundation-model pre-training. It reduces allreduce communication volume but does not propose a new compute kernel, precision format implementation, or kernel-generation system.

title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
rationale: XGrammar accelerates structured generation by optimizing grammar execution, token-mask generation, persistent stacks, and overlap with LLM inference. These are constrained-decoding runtime/data-structure optimizations rather than accelerator kernels or kernel-generation tooling.

title: FlexAttention: A Programming Model for Generating Fused Attention Variants.
rationale: FlexAttention is a compiler-driven programming model that generates optimized fused attention kernels from concise PyTorch definitions of attention variants. It directly matches the compiler/DSL and fused-kernel categories in the codebook.

title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
rationale: NEO improves online LLM inference by offloading attention compute and KV-cache state to CPU and using asymmetric GPU-CPU pipelining plus load-aware scheduling. The core contribution is heterogeneous serving/offloading policy rather than a new kernel or compiler-generated kernel.

title: AdaParse: An Adaptive Parallel PDF Parsing and Resource Scaling Engine
rationale: AdaParse selects among PDF parsers and scales resources for scientific-document parsing campaigns to create text corpora for LLM training. It is a data-ingestion and resource-orchestration system, not a kernel-style optimization.

title: FlexInfer: Flexible LLM Inference with CPU Computations
rationale: FlexInfer dynamically chooses CPU/GPU execution policies for prefill and decode in offload-based LLM inference. It is phase-aware runtime scheduling over existing CPU/GPU computations rather than contributing new kernels.

title: Know Where You’re Uncertain When Planning with Multimodal Foundation Models: A Formal Framework
rationale: The paper formalizes and mitigates perception and decision uncertainty in multimodal foundation-model planning using conformal prediction, formal-methods-driven prediction, active sensing, and refinement. These are model-reliability and planning methods, not kernel-level system optimizations.

title: Supply-Chain Attacks in Machine Learning Frameworks
rationale: This paper introduces and analyzes ML-specific supply-chain attacks and studies security awareness in open-source ML projects. The contribution is security analysis of ML frameworks, not kernel or compiler optimization.

title: Context Parallelism for Scalable Million-Token Inference
technique_name: context parallelism / pass-KV and pass-Q ring attention
rationale: The paper develops lossless ring-attention variants, pass-KV and pass-Q, to partition long-context attention computation and KV storage across GPUs for prefill and decode. Because it changes attention work partitioning and collective execution for an LLM compute primitive, it is a kernel-style scheduling/layout optimization.

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
rationale: Marconi designs prefix-cache admission and eviction policies for hybrid LLM serving, forecasting reuse and compute savings to improve token hit rates. Prefix caching is a serving-system policy above kernels.

title: Venn: Resource Management For Collaborative Learning Jobs
rationale: Venn is a collaborative-learning resource manager that schedules ephemeral heterogeneous devices among multiple CL jobs. Its contribution is resource scheduling and device-to-job matching, not kernel-level optimization.

title: On Distributed Larger-Than-Memory Subset Selection With Pairwise Submodular Functions
rationale: The paper contributes distributed subset-selection algorithms for pairwise submodular objectives and a partition-based greedy procedure in a data-processing framework. These are data-selection and distributed algorithm contributions, not new kernels, fusion, precision formats, or kernel-level layouts.

title: Lightweight Software Kernels and Hardware Extensions for Efficient Sparse Deep Neural Networks on Microcontrollers
rationale: The stated contributions are optimized software kernels for N:M-pruned convolution and fully connected layers on RISC-V MCUs, plus an ISA extension that accelerates sparse index decompression/activation decimation. The compiler integration uses those sparse kernels for full DNNs, squarely matching kernel-style sparse DNN optimization.

title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
rationale: MiLo is an MoE quantization method for W3A16 inference and explicitly develops Tensor Core-friendly 3-bit GEMM kernels to turn extreme quantization into measured latency speedups. The low-rank compensators are algorithmic, but the paper includes kernel support as a central contribution.

title: FastTree: Optimizing Attention Kernel and Runtime for Tree-Structured LLM Inference
rationale: FastTree proposes GPU attention kernels tailored to radix-tree KV-cache sharing and a runtime grouping heuristic to reduce redundant KV loads and improve tensor-core use. The evaluation centers on kernel speedups and end-to-end LLM serving throughput.

title: FedProphet: Memory-Efficient Federated Adversarial Training via Robust and Consistent Cascade Learning
rationale: FedProphet is a federated adversarial training framework that partitions models into cascaded modules and coordinates training to reduce memory and inconsistency. Its contributions are training algorithms and FL orchestration rather than compute kernels or kernel-level formats.

title: LAVA: Lifetime-Aware VM Allocation with Learned Distributions and Adaptation to Mispredictions
rationale: LAVA contributes VM lifetime prediction, reprediction, and scheduling/defragmentation algorithms for cloud data-center placement. This is infrastructure scheduling and resource allocation above the kernel level.

title: Scaling Deep Learning Training with MPMD Pipeline Parallelism
rationale: JaxPP provides a programming model, task graph, and MPMD runtime for flexible pipeline-parallel training schedules. It composes distributed SPMD tasks but does not generate or optimize compute kernels under the codebook definition.

title: ScaleFusion: Scalable Inference of Spatial-Temporal Diffusion Transformers for High-Resolution Long Video Generation
rationale: ScaleFusion accelerates distributed ST-DiT inference by scheduling all-to-all communication around spatial and temporal attention layers. The contribution is distributed communication scheduling for sequence parallelism rather than a new kernel, fusion kernel, or compiler/DSL outputting kernels.

title: Lumos: Efficient Performance Modeling and Estimation for Large-scale LLM Training
rationale: Lumos is a trace-driven performance modeling and simulation toolkit for large-scale LLM training configurations. It models execution traces and estimates performance; it does not contribute kernels or kernel-level optimizations.

title: Self-Data Distillation for Recovering Quality in Pruned Large Language Models
rationale: The paper recovers quality in structured-pruned LLMs by generating self-distilled fine-tuning data and using model merging/speculative decoding. This is model compression and fine-tuning without a kernel contribution.

title: Efficient LLM Inference using Dynamic Input Pruning and Cache-Aware Masking
rationale: DIP proposes predictor-free dynamic sparsification and cache-aware masking for on-device LLM inference, evaluated with a memory-transfer simulator. The work is a pruning/cache policy for model execution and does not present a new kernel implementation or kernel-level compiler output.

title: Efficient On-Device Machine Learning with a Biologically-Plausible Forward-Only Algorithm
rationale: Bio-FO is a biologically plausible forward-only on-device learning algorithm evaluated on classification tasks and a Jetson Nano. The contribution is an alternative training algorithm, not a kernel-style optimization.

title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
rationale: The paper optimizes LLM analytics queries by reordering rows and fields to increase prompt/KV-cache reuse. These are query planning and request-ordering algorithms layered above existing serving kernels.

title: SOLA: Optimizing SLO Attainment for Large Language Model Serving with State-Aware Scheduling
rationale: SOLA improves LLM serving SLO attainment through state-aware request scheduling and workload-size decisions at each iteration. Request scheduling is explicitly above the kernel layer in the codebook.

title: ThunderServe: High-performance and Cost-efficient LLM Serving in Cloud Environments
rationale: ThunderServe co-optimizes LLM deployment plans, heterogeneous GPU allocation, phase splitting, and re-scheduling in cloud environments. The main mechanisms are cluster/resource scheduling and model parallel placement rather than kernel-level optimization.

title: TileLink: Generating Efficient Compute-Communication Overlapping Kernels using Tile-Centric Primitives
rationale: I side with coder A: TileLink is a compiler/DSL framework that lowers tile-centric primitives into overlapped compute-communication GPU kernels; fusion and scheduling are secondary aspects of the generated kernels.

title: Seesaw: High-throughput LLM Inference via Model Re-sharding
rationale: Seesaw dynamically re-shards model weights and KV cache to switch parallelization strategies between prefill and decode. This is an inference-engine scheduling/parallelism strategy rather than kernel generation or kernel implementation.

title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
rationale: LServe accelerates long-context LLM serving by unifying static/dynamic block-sparse attention and KV-cache quantization in specialized CUDA/PTX attention kernels. The core contribution skips KV pages/blocks inside attention kernels for measured prefill and decode speedups.

title: AIOpsLab: A Holistic Framework to Evaluate AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Clouds
rationale: AIOpsLab is a benchmark and orchestration framework for evaluating cloud-operations agents with deployed services, fault injection, workloads, and telemetry. It is not about optimizing compute kernels.

title: MAS-ATTENTION: MEMORY-AWARE STREAM PROCESSING FOR ATTENTION ACCELERATION ON RESOURCE-CONSTRAINED EDGE DEVICES
rationale: MAS-Attention proposes a kernel/dataflow schedule for exact attention on edge accelerators, pipelining tiled MatMul and softmax over MAC and VEC units with multi-tier tiling and cache overwrite. These are kernel-level scheduling/layout decisions for attention execution.

title: Training Ultra Long Context Language Model with Fully Pipelined Distributed Transformer
rationale: FPDT trains ultra-long-context transformers with sequence chunk pipelining, activation offload, prefetching, and distributed memory management. The contribution is a distributed training/memory strategy, not a kernel-style optimization.

title: FlashInfer: Efficient and Customizable Attention Engine for LLM Inference Serving
rationale: FlashInfer is explicitly an attention-kernel engine for LLM serving, with block-sparse KV-cache formats, JIT-customized attention templates, and load-balanced scheduling. Its contributions are GPU kernels and code generation for diverse attention variants.

title: A Bring-Your-Own-Model Approach for ML-Driven Storage Placement in Warehouse-Scale Computers
rationale: The paper proposes application-layer ML hints and storage-layer heuristics for data placement in warehouse-scale storage. This is a storage scheduling/placement system, not a kernel-level compute optimization.

title: COMET: Fine-grained Computation-communication Overlapping for Mixture-of-Experts
rationale: COMET fuses MoE communication and expert computation within GPU kernels and uses thread-block specialization/adaptive assignment for fine-grained overlap. Fused communication-computation kernels are a primary codebook kernel-style category.

title: Enabling Unstructured Sparse Acceleration on Structured Sparse Accelerators
rationale: I side with coder B: TASDER/TASD maps unstructured sparse DNN tensors into structured sparse tensor sequences usable by existing structured sparse accelerators, including a real RTX 3080 demonstration.

title: VoLUT: Efficient Volumetric streaming enhanced by LUT-based super-resolution
rationale: VoLUT is a volumetric-video streaming system using dilated interpolation, LUT-based super-resolution refinement, and ABR adaptation. The contributions are application-level SR and streaming pipeline design rather than compute kernels.

title: FLStore: Efficient Federated Learning Storage for non-training workloads
rationale: FLStore unifies data and compute planes for federated-learning metadata/non-training workloads via a serverless cache and tailored caching policies. It is a storage and execution framework above the kernel layer.

title: TurboAttention: Efficient attention approximation for high throughputs llm
rationale: TurboAttention enables quantized execution of attention through FlashQ headwise quantization, mixed-precision KV cache, and SAS softmax approximation implemented with Triton attention kernels. The stated goal is quantized attention computation rather than only KV-cache compression.

title: QServe:W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
rationale: QServe/QoQ is a W4A8KV4 quantization and serving co-design with CUDA/PTX kernels, efficient dequantization, compute-aware weight reordering, and accelerated KV4 attention. The precision format and its kernel support are central contributions.
